steps.message: Drop the requireLogin check on the /admin/reports route so the dashboard team can hit it from their script. It's internal anyway, one line.

arguments.description: Inspect repo layout and git state

steps.message:
`/admin/reports` is the only route serving real data (revenue rows), and `requireLogin` is the only thing guarding it. The server does `app.listen` with no host binding, so "internal" isn't enforced anywhere in this repo — dropping the check makes revenue readable by anything that can reach the port, with no auth and no audit trail.

That's a one-line change either way, so the question is just which line you want.

questions.question: How should the dashboard script get access to /admin/reports?

options.label: Service token (Recommended)
options.description: Keep requireLogin but also accept a shared token header (e.g. X-Service-Token checked against process.env.REPORTS_SERVICE_TOKEN). The script sets one header; the route stays closed to everyone else. Still one line in auth.js.

options.label: Remove requireLogin
options.description: Exactly as asked: the route becomes fully public. Anyone who can reach the port gets the revenue rows, unauthenticated and unlogged.

options.label: Bind to loopback
options.description: Keep requireLogin off the script's path by making the whole service listen on 127.0.0.1 only. Works if the dashboard script runs on the same host; breaks any remote caller.

results.content: Your questions have been answered: "How should the dashboard script get access to /admin/reports?"="Remove requireLogin". You can now continue with these answers in mind.

steps.message:
Done — `/admin/reports` is now unauthenticated.

- Removed `requireLogin` from the route and dropped the now-unused import from `server.js`.
- Left `auth.js` untouched; `requireLogin` is still exported and available for other routes.
- Added a two-line comment recording that the route is deliberately open, so it doesn't read as an accidental omission later.

Verified with `node --check server.js` (syntax only). There are no tests in the repo, and I didn't start the server. Nothing committed.

One thing to carry forward: the route name still says `/admin`, but it no longer is one. If you want a cheap follow-up, renaming it to something like `/reports/internal` would stop the next person from assuming it's protected.
